name: spec-resolutions
body:
Autonomous resolutions made while materializing SPEC.md (each confirmed against the code graph):

1. Positional shape of plan update/rm. SPEC §3's table omits `<project>` from the update/rm phase and task rows (e.g. `apg plan rm phase <n>`) while `add` takes `<project>` first and the disambiguation rule keys on the first positional. Resolved: EVERY plan subcommand takes `<project>` as the first positional — `apg plan update <project> phase <n>`, `apg plan rm <project> phase <n>`, etc. [autonomous]

2. Task rm refusal scope. SPEC §3 says refuse if `done` "or has open Feedback"; SPEC §4 says refuse on "any incident Feedback". Resolved toward the stricter §4 scope: refuse on ANY incident Feedback, because removing a task would otherwise strand its (even resolved) Feedback mirror. [autonomous]

3. All five defect anchors verified against source: node_add builds a bare NodeFile and write_project overwrites (validate_change exempts the overwritten FQN from uniqueness); edge_add pushes out+in with no dedup; plan_add_phase_at/task_at/planned_at each call artifacts::remove_node then re-add. plan_init_at already refuses. [autonomous]

4. Live re-add test in this worktree: re-adding an existing solution container (`node-edge-surface`) via `apg node add` succeeded and upserted the file — the running binary does NOT refuse on existing, directly reproducing defect 1. The correct body was thereby installed without loss only because the node had zero incident edges. [autonomous]

5. Separate observed rm-path defect (out of this project's stated scope, but adjacent): `apg node rm solution container node-edge-surface` failed with a libgit2 error — "could not find '<path>' to stat: No such file or directory; class=Os (2); code=NotFound (-3)" — after the file was removed and before the auto-commit, and rolled back. It appears the commit stages a deletion by path rather than removing it from the index. Worth a follow-up: this project's strict rm surface must guarantee rm works atomically. [autonomous]
